sections.content: How many people are "production and process engineers"?

34,305 people

were counted on the census as "production and process engineers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Production and process engineers advise on and direct technical aspects of production programmes to ensure cost-effectiveness and efficiency.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "production and process engineers" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "production and process engineers", 14.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "production and process engineers" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "production and process engineers" included:

  • business associate professionals (other)
  • medical and dental technicians
  • electronics engineers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "production and process engineers" there were more men than women (78.8% compared with 21.2%).

This means "production and process engineers" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "science, research, engineering and technology professionals".

Men made up 78.8% and women made up 21.2% of "production and process engineers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "production and process engineers" included:

  • production managers and directors in manufacturing
  • parking and civil enforcement occupations
  • chemical and related process operatives

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "production and process engineers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "production and process engineers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "production and process engineers", 6.9% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (91.2% compared with 8.8%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (91.7%) than self-employed (8.3%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
